title: Potato Gnocchi
subtitle: Light Italian potato dumplings with butter and sage
excerpt: Pillowy, light potato gnocchi made with floury potatoes, a minimum of flour, and no egg, tossed in sage butter until the outside has a faint, golden crust and the inside stays cloud-soft. The great test of Italian kitchen instinct.

recipe.sourceNotes: Potato gnocchi (gnocchi di patate) are a Roman and Northern Italian staple, traditionally served on Thursdays in Rome (giovedì gnocchi — 'Thursday gnocchi'). The dish requires a precise touch: too much flour produces dense, stodgy dumplings; too little means they fall apart in the cooking water. The key principles are: use floury potatoes (Maris Piper or King Edward), bake or steam rather than boil them to minimise water content, and work the dough as little as possible. The best gnocchi are slightly sticky and require confidence: over-flouring a dough that feels too sticky will make it tough. The sage butter sauce is the classic accompaniment in Northern Italy; in Southern Italy gnocchi is more often served with tomato sauce.

content.text: Bake the potatoes rather than boiling them; boiled potatoes absorb water and require more flour to compensate, making the gnocchi heavier. Rice the potatoes while hot and leave to steam-dry for 5 minutes before adding the flour. Work the dough quickly and as little as possible. Cook a test gnocco before shaping the whole batch; if it falls apart in the water, add a little more flour.

items.preparation: floury variety (Maris Piper or King Edward); baked whole at 200°C for 1 hour
optional; adds richness; makes the dough slightly easier to work

content.text: Scoop the hot baked potato flesh from the skins. Rice immediately or press through a potato ricer onto a lightly floured surface. Leave to steam-dry for 5 minutes. Mix the flour, parmesan, and salt into the potato. Add the egg if using. Work quickly into a soft dough; it will be slightly sticky. Do not over-work.

Divide the dough into portions. Roll each into a long rope about 2 cm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut into 3 cm pieces. Roll each piece over a fork to create ridges if desired. Place on a floured tray.

Cook the gnocchi in well-salted boiling water; they are done 30 seconds after they float to the surface. Meanwhile, brown the butter with the sage leaves until the butter smells nutty. Drain the gnocchi and add directly to the brown butter. Toss to coat. Serve with extra parmesan.
